lines.text: But if we are not prepared to accept the possibility of in-
gratitude and disappointment, we shall never experience the
rich rewards of love and confidence.
Just as arrogance which insists on its rights corrupts the
life both of the individual and the community, so also it is
arrogance which in times of sore distress arouses a spirit of
complaint and accusation, and prevents sorrow from bearing
the fruits of grace. No doubt there are haughty and defiant
men who are steeled by suffering. But are they really
matured thereby? There is a defiant harshness of character
which chooses self-isolation and reserve, and which conceals
an inner cold-heartedness and spiritual void. It may well be
that such a man is invulnerable to the blows of fate; but he
is also blind to the graciousness of fate. There is also a
character which is steeled by heavy sorrow and which is
truly matured and strengthened thereby, a character of
cheerful open-heartedness, of inner spiritual wealth; a
character which gives itself freely to all, in warmth of heart
which radiates itself on all with whom it comes into contact.
This is genuine power, whereas cold harshness is only
apparent power and behind its reserve hides an inner weak-
ness. Genuine strength of character does not fortify itself
against fate in an attitude of proud reserve, but exposes itself
to fate in the confidence that whatever fate brings can only
make it grow stronger and richer. Such a man understands
and accepts his destiny as a real source of grace and blessing.
Moreover he has the inner freedom of spirit to enjoy the
beautiful and the good which do come to him, the sunny
days through which it is granted him to pass, in a spirit of
serenity, without fear and without a bad conscience. For
were we not resigned to whatever destiny may bring, how
could we with a good conscience enjoy the good which is
granted us, when all around us there is so much distress and
misery? How could we, especially in a time like this, have
a good conscience and inner peace, we who live at home in
security (or at least the majority of us) no doubt with many
cares and troubles yet at the same time free from the super-
